summary: 1968 Aermotor tower built by the Alabama Forestry Commission at Monte Sano State Park; taken down and rebuilt at Fire Tower Camp near Crane Hill, reported Sept 2025.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor tower with 7 by 7 foot metal cab, galvanized steel
facts.status_note: No longer at Monte Sano State Park. Alabama Living reported in September 2025 that it had been taken down and was being rebuilt at Fire Tower Camp near Crane Hill, Cullman County. The camp's hiking page describes it as restored.
facts.agency: Alabama Forestry Commission (built 1968); State of Alabama, Monte Sano State Park (administrator per NHLR); Fire Tower Camp (current site per Alabama Living)

access.note: Stands on the grounds of Fire Tower Camp near Crane Hill. The camp invites visitors to climb it; the sources give no hours, fees or rules.

visit.trail_note: Listed on the camp's hiking page with its other trails and landmarks. Check with the camp before going.

corrections.proposed: standing, relocated to Fire Tower Camp, Crane Hill, Cullman County
corrections.why: Alabama Living (Sept 2025) reports the tower was taken down at Monte Sano and rebuilt at Fire Tower Camp; the camp's hiking page describes it as restored.
Madison is the county of the former Monte Sano site; the tower now stands in Cullman County.
NHLR gives 100 ft, which is 30.5 m. The 30.0 figure is a rounded value; the 109 ft figure on the camp's site is not reconciled.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and the 2025 Alabama Living article describe a 100-foot tower; the camp's hiking page describes the restored tower as 109 feet. The sources do not say whether the rebuild changed the height, so the Register figure is kept as the original design height.

The Register and the marker say the lookout was used in the 1950s by NASA to track Sputnik and Explorer telemetry. The 1968 tower is later than that, so the claim most likely refers to the earlier wooden lookout. No source says so directly, and the story says so.
The 2025 article says visitors could not climb the tower at Monte Sano. The camp's site invites visitors to climb it. Both can be true because the tower moved; no source gives hours, fees or rules.

notes_for_editor: The brief's record is out of date: it lists the tower as standing at Monte Sano State Park with coordinates there. Alabama Living (Sept 2025) reports it was taken down and rebuilt at Fire Tower Camp near Crane Hill in Cullman County. The camp's hiking page (undated) says climb the restored 109 ft tower, and the camp home page confirms rentals; the exact opening date and current climbing status are not confirmed. The 109 ft vs 100 ft height gap is unresolved. A Facebook snippet (not fetched, so not cited) gives a 2022 end date at Monte Sano and says the tower was sold; this is unverified and left out of the story. The Instagram posts from Feb 2026 said the tower was not yet finished; those were search snippets only and are not cited. The NASA telemetry claim is in both the Register and the marker; the 1950s date predates the 1968 tower. Coordinates not updated (no source gives the new site). No photos added; none were checked for license.
